Package neqsim.process.equipment.reactor

Class AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationTrajectory

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.reactor.AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationTrajectory
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationTrajectory extends Object implements Serializable
Exact piecewise-constant exposure trajectory for the published aqueous total-sulfide/O2 screening correlation.

Each segment delegates its rate calculation to AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationKinetics. The total-sulfide fraction therefore follows exp(-sum(k_i [O2]_i dt_i)) without numerical timestep error. The reported one-standard-deviation log-rate scatter is propagated as one common multiplicative correlation envelope.

This class neither consumes oxygen nor assigns sulfur products. It does not accept pressure and does not qualify a dense-phase CO2 or pipeline calculation.

1.0

NeqSim Team

    • advance

      public static AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationTrajectory.Result advance(double initialTotalSulfideMolality, List<AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationTrajectory.Segment> segments)
      Propagate total dissolved sulfide through ordered constant-state exposure segments.
      Parameters:
      initialTotalSulfideMolality - initial total-sulfide molality [mol/kg water]
      segments - non-empty ordered exposure segments
      Returns:
      immutable trajectory result with per-segment evidence
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when the initial molality is outside the source experiment, the segment list is null or empty, a segment is null, or an accumulated value is not finite

    • timeToRemainingFractionRange

      public static AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationTrajectory.TargetCrossingRangeResult timeToRemainingFractionRange(double targetRemainingFraction, List<AqueousHydrogenSulfideOxidationTrajectory.Segment> segments)
      Locate the first time a remaining-total-sulfide target is reached within ordered exposure segments.

      The calculation analytically inverts cumulative exposure for the lower, nominal, and upper rates. All three fit-scatter paths must reach the requested target within the supplied finite trajectory. The result therefore never extrapolates the final segment or returns an infinite crossing time.

      Parameters:
      targetRemainingFraction - target total-sulfide fraction in the interval (0, 1]
      segments - non-empty ordered exposure segments
      Returns:
      immutable shortest, nominal, and longest target-crossing evidence
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when the target or trajectory is invalid, a calculated value is not finite, or the target is not reached for every fit-scatter path
